name: Leaf salad
summary: A platter of forest and garden leaves that you roll into a funnel around boiled pork, shrimp, and pork skin, then eat in one bite. Each mouthful runs hot, sour, salty, sweet, astringent, and nutty at once.
origin: Kon Tum’s leaf salad, eaten year-round on Trần Cao Vân.
taste: Sour mango leaf, nutty sung leaf, and astringent guava leaf sit side by side, so the bite changes with the leaves you pick.
howToEat: Roll a large leaf, such as sung, perilla, mustard green, or lettuce, into a funnel. Add five to seven more leaves, then pork, shrimp, pork skin rubbed with roasted rice powder, a spoon of sauce, salt, and pepper, and eat it in one bite.

Platters and fillings vary by kitchen. Publishers count from about 30 to 70 kinds of leaf, and they disagree on whether the rainy or the dry season brings the fuller platter. Some kitchens add carp or rice paper. The sauce is built on fermented glutinous rice, dried shrimp, and pork belly, and may carry mẹ, satay, or the smell of wine lees.
where: Trần Cao Vân, Kon Tum city, known as phố gỏi lá, the leaf-salad street. Go at lunch or dinner.
seoTitle: Goi la in Kon Tum — leaf salad on Tran Cao Van
seoDescription: Roll forest and garden leaves around pork, shrimp, and pork skin and eat it in one bite. The platters are on Trần Cao Vân, Kon Tum’s leaf-salad street.
priceBand: 100,000–150,000 VND a platter for 3–4 (VietnamNet); about 300,000–400,000 VND for 6–8 (Vietnam News Agency); 350,000–600,000 VND for 4–6 (Go Vietnam)
